easy.def: A soft, warm bed cover filled with feathers.
examples: The eiderdown is warm.
I snuggled under the eiderdown.
The bed has an eiderdown.

more.def: A warm quilt filled with soft feathers from the eider duck.
examples: She snuggled under the eiderdown on a cold night.
The eiderdown kept the baby warm.
Grandma's bed had a red eiderdown.
I have eight crayons.
A spider has eight legs.
My brother is eight.

more.def: The number 8, which comes after seven and before nine.
examples: An octopus has eight arms.
The bus left at eight o'clock.
She scored eight points.
My sister is eighteen.
I have eighteen blocks.
Eighteen kids rode the bus.

more.def: The number 18, which comes after seventeen and before nineteen.
examples: A person is usually an adult at eighteen.
The path around the lake is eighteen miles long.
The class has eighteen desks in three rows.
It is her eighteenth birthday.
He came eighteenth.
It was the eighteenth day.

more.def: Coming after the seventeenth and before the nineteenth.
examples: My cousin will celebrate her eighteenth birthday in June.
He finished in eighteenth place.
The eighteenth chapter was the funniest.
I am eighth in line.
The eighth day is Monday.
She finished eighth.

more.def: Coming after the seventh one and before the ninth one.
examples: He finished eighth in the race.
My cousin is in eighth grade.
The eighth chapter is short.
I ate an eighth of the pizza.
An eighth is small.
Cut it in eighths.

more.def: One of eight equal parts that make a whole.
examples: Each of us got an eighth of the pie.
An eighth of the class is absent.
The recipe needs an eighth of a teaspoon.

easy.def: The number 80, which is eight tens.
examples: Grandpa is eighty.
I counted to eighty.
The bus holds eighty people.

more.def: The number 80, which comes after seventy-nine.
examples: My great-grandmother just turned eighty years old.
Eighty children came to the school fair.
We drove eighty miles to the lake.
You can have either of the two apples.
Either of us can carry the box.
I do not mind either.

more.def: One or the other of two people or things; it does not matter which.
examples: There are two paths, and either leads to the lake.
Either of my sisters can help you with math.
You can have tea or juice, and I will take either.

easy.def: Used with "or" to show a choice.
examples: We can either swim or play ball.
Either Mia or Sam will lead.
You can either walk or ride.

more.def: Used before the first of two choices that are joined by "or".
examples: You can either call me tonight or send a message in the morning.
Either the red scarf or the blue one will match your coat.
We will either take the bus or walk to the museum.
I do not like peas, and Ben does not either.
She cannot swim, and I cannot either.
It is not hot, and it is not cold either.

more.def: Used after a negative statement to mean "also not".
examples: He did not finish his homework, and I did not either.
The store did not have milk, and it did not have eggs either.
The old bridge was not safe, and the path was not either.
